t.6.16.1: When Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, had crossed the ocean together with his army, the glorious Rāvaṇa spoke to his two ministers, Śuka and Sāraṇa.
t.6.16.2: The monkey army has crossed the entire ocean, so hard to cross; this bridge built by Rāma across the ocean is something never seen before.
t.6.16.3: I could in no way believe in the building of a bridge across the ocean; yet that army of monkeys must certainly be reckoned by me.
t.6.16.4: You two, entering the army of the monkeys unnoticed, must learn its size and its strength, and who are the chief among the monkeys.
t.6.16.6: And how that bridge was built across the ocean, that vast expanse of waters, and how those great-souled monkeys were encamped.
t.6.16.5: Those who are the counsellors esteemed by Rāma and by Sugrīva, those who advance in the forefront, and those monkeys who are valiant heroes.
t.6.16.7: You should find out truly the resolve of Rāma, his valor and his weapons, and those of the heroic Lakṣmaṇa as well.
t.6.16.8: And who is the commander of those mighty vānaras? Having learned this exactly as it is, you two should return quickly.
t.6.16.9: Thus instructed, the two heroic rākṣasas Śuka and Sāraṇa, assuming the form of monkeys, entered the monkey army.
t.6.16.10: Then the two, Śuka and Sāraṇa, were unable to count that army of monkeys, inconceivable in size and making the hair stand on end.
t.6.16.11: That army was stationed on the mountain peaks, in the caves and in the caverns, on the shores of the ocean, in the forests and in the groves.
t.6.16.12: The mighty army, raising a terrifying roar, was everywhere crossing, had crossed, and was eager to cross; it was encamped and still settling into camp.
t.6.16.13: The mighty Vibhīṣaṇa saw those two in disguise and seized Śuka and Sāraṇa. He then told Rāma: “These two spies, conquerors of enemy cities, have come here from Laṅkā.”
t.6.16.14: Then, seeing Rāma, the two, distressed and despairing of their lives, frightened and with palms joined in supplication, spoke these words.
t.6.16.15: O gentle one, O delight of the Raghus, we two have come here, both sent by Rāvaṇa, to learn the full extent of this entire army of yours.
t.6.16.16: Having heard those words of the two, Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, who delighted in the welfare of all beings, spoke these words with a smile.
t.6.16.17: If you have seen the entire army, or if we have been thoroughly examined, or if the task has been done as you were instructed, then you may go back as you please.
t.6.16.18: Having entered the city of Laṅkā, you two must tell the king of the Rākṣasas, the younger brother of Dhanada, my words exactly as they were spoken.
t.6.16.19: Relying on that strength by which you carried off my Sītā, display it now as you please, together with your army and your kinsmen.
t.6.16.20: Tomorrow, at the proper time, behold the city of Laṅkā with its ramparts and its gateways, and the army of the rākṣasas, destroyed by me with my arrows.
t.6.16.21: Tomorrow I shall unleash my terrible wrath, as Vāsava, wielder of the thunderbolt, hurls his thunderbolt upon the Dānavas; summon up your strength, Rāvaṇa!
t.6.16.22: Thus instructed in reply, the two rākṣasas Śuka and Sāraṇa came to the city of Laṅkā and spoke to the lord of the rākṣasas.
t.6.16.23: O lord of the rākṣasas, we two, seized by Vibhīṣaṇa and deserving of death, were set free by the righteous-souled Rāma of immeasurable splendour once he had seen us.
t.6.16.24: Where four bulls among men are gathered together in one place, heroes like the guardians of the world, skilled in weapons and firm in valor...
t.6.16.25: The glorious Rāma, son of Daśaratha, and Lakṣmaṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa, and Sugrīva of great splendor, whose valor equals that of mighty Indra.
t.6.16.26: These are capable of uprooting the city of Laṅkā, with its ramparts and its gateways, and carrying it elsewhere. Let all the monkeys stand ready.
t.6.16.27: Such is the form of that Rāma, and such are his weapons, that he alone will destroy the city of Laṅkā; let those three others stand aside.
t.6.16.28: That army, guarded by Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa and by Sugrīva, became even more unassailable, even by all the gods and asuras together.
t.6.16.29: The army of the high-souled forest-dwellers, who now desire to fight, is in a state of great delight. Enough of hostility; let peace be made, and let Maithilī be given back to Dāśarathi.
